topic_tag: a posthumous novel and its editor
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: In a study published decades later, one scholar argued that this editor had ______ the book.

worlds.passage: When a novelist died in 1931, she left the manuscript of her last novel, a story of dockworkers' families set in the 1880s, to her longtime editor. A burst pipe had soaked the trunk it lay in, and most of its pages had run gray and blurred. The editor spent the next three years on those pages alone. A scholar who later set the book printed in 1934 beside the novelist's letters, which describe it scene by scene, found nearly every scene there, with a few short gaps where lines were lost. In a study published decades later, one scholar argued that this editor had ______ the book.
worlds.explanation: The pages were ruined when found, the editor worked on them for three years, and the printed book turned out to contain nearly every scene the novelist described, so the editor "salvaged" the book. "Sanitized" fails because nearly every scene survives; nothing was cut for propriety. "Shelved" fails because the three years went into work on the pages, after which the book was printed. "Updated" fails because the only differences from the novelist's plan are lines lost to the water.

sanitized.why: the book matches the novelist's own description, so nothing was cut to make it respectable

shelved.quote: spent the next three years on those pages alone
shelved.why: the delay was spent working on the text, not leaving it aside

updated.quote: a few short gaps where lines were lost
updated.why: the only departures from the novel are losses from damage, not changes that bring it up to date

worlds.passage: When a novelist died in 1931, she left the manuscript of her last novel, a story of dockworkers' families set in the 1880s, to her longtime editor. In the manuscript, which survives intact in the editor's papers, a daughter runs up card debts, the strikers curse their foreman, and one chapter is set in a tavern. The book the editor printed the following spring keeps every chapter and every character; in it the daughter owes a dressmaker, the strikers call their foreman "sir," and that chapter is set in a tea shop. In a study published decades later, one scholar argued that this editor had ______ the book.
worlds.explanation: Only by setting the manuscript beside the book does the pattern appear: every change swaps something a reader of the time might find improper (gambling, cursing, a tavern) for something respectable, so the editor "sanitized" the book. "Salvaged" fails because the manuscript was intact and needed no rescue. "Shelved" fails because the book was printed the spring after the novelist died. "Updated" fails because the replacements belong to the same period as the originals; nothing was moved closer to the present.

salvaged.quote: survives intact in the editor's papers
salvaged.why: the manuscript was intact, so the editor's work was altering it, not rescuing it

shelved.why: the book was published at once rather than set aside

updated.quote: keeps every chapter and every character
updated.why: the story and its people stay in the 1880s; a dressmaker and a tea shop belong to that period as much as a card table and a tavern, so only propriety changed

worlds.passage: When a novelist died in 1931, she left the manuscript of her last novel, a story of dockworkers' families set in the 1880s, to her longtime editor. The editor told her family it was her best book, and for twenty years told anyone who asked that it needed more time. The editor's press printed four other dockside novels in those years. The editor's diaries mention the manuscript only once, when it was moved with a desk to a new office, and it was printed from that desk in 1953, after the editor's death. In a study published decades later, one scholar argued that this editor had ______ the book.
worlds.explanation: The editor praised the book, kept putting off its publication for twenty years while printing rivals, and by the diaries' account never worked on it, so the editor "shelved" the book. "Salvaged" fails because the manuscript faced no danger. "Sanitized" and "updated" both fail because the editor never worked on the text at all: it went from the desk to the printer after the editor's death.

salvaged.quote: moved with a desk to a new office
salvaged.why: the manuscript simply sat in a desk; there was no damage or loss to rescue it from

sanitized.why: in twenty years the editor recorded no work on the text, so nothing was cut

updated.quote: printed from that desk in 1953, after the editor's death
updated.why: the text went to print untouched by the editor, so it was not brought up to date

worlds.passage: When a novelist died in 1931, she left the manuscript of her last novel, a story of dockworkers' families set in the 1880s, to her longtime editor. The editor printed it in 1932. Its characters keep the names, quarrels, and fates the manuscript gives them, and every chapter is present. Reviewers, none of whom knew of the manuscript, praised the book as a faithful picture of the waterfront as they themselves knew it, down to the cranes and the closing strike, which ends, as the great strike of 1926 had, in the men's defeat. In a study published decades later, one scholar argued that this editor had ______ the book.
worlds.explanation: The manuscript is set in the 1880s, yet reviewers in 1932 recognized the printed book as their own waterfront, down to its strike of 1926, while its characters and chapters are unchanged; combining these shows the editor moved the setting forward, so the editor "updated" the book. "Salvaged" fails because nothing was damaged or lost. "Sanitized" fails because the characters' quarrels and fates were kept. "Shelved" fails because the book was printed the year after the novelist died.

salvaged.why: an intact text was reworked, not rescued from damage

sanitized.quote: keep the names, quarrels, and fates
sanitized.why: the characters' conduct was left as written, so nothing was cleaned up

shelved.why: the editor published within a year rather than setting the book aside
